table_B1_minimum_scheduling_radius_and_e.description: Minimum radius for scheduling (r), minimum diameter of bending former (M = 2r), and minimum end projection (P) by nominal bar size. P is split into general case and link-with-bend-<150deg case.
notes: 'a' flag = minimum end projection for smaller bars is governed by bending practicalities, not the general formula.
General P column applies min 5d straight, including links where bend >=150deg.
Link P column (bend < 150deg) requires min 10d straight.
additional_notes: Note 1: due to spring-back, actual bend radius will be slightly greater than half the diameter of former.
Note 2: BS4449:2005 grade B500A in sizes below 8mm does not conform to BS EN 1992-1-1:2004.

bar_areas_by_number_and_size.description: Cross-sectional steel area (mm2) for N bars of a given nominal diameter.
bar_areas_by_number_and_size.derivable: Every value in this table equals N x pi x (d/2)^2, so it is DERIVED/computable rather than needing verbatim storage; retained here as-given for source fidelity, but a generator should compute it rather than look it up.

bar_areas_by_pitch_and_size.description: Steel area per metre width (mm2/m) for a given bar pitch and size. Used for slabs/walls/mesh.

bar_weights_by_pitch_and_size.description: Steel weight per unit area (kg/m2) for a given bar pitch and size.

fabric_types_BS4483.description: Preferred steel fabric (mesh) types per BS4483:1985.
fabric_types_BS4483.note: Wire of Grade 500 to BS4449/BS4482 used except wrapping fabric wire may be Grade 250. 5mm size available in hard-drawn wire only. 6/7/8/10/12mm available in hard-drawn wire or bar form. 7mm not a preferred cold-worked bar size.

effective_anchorage_length_L_bars.description: Effective anchorage length (mm) measured from start of bend, for an L-bar (90-degree hook), by mandrel-size/bar-diameter ratio and bar size.

variables.mandrel_dia: bending mandrel diameter, expressed as a multiple of bar dia in the row index

effective_anchorage_length_L_bars.note: First data cell (mandrel ratio 4, bar 8mm = 102) appears anomalously low relative to the progression of the rest of the row/column and may be an OCR/scan artifact from the source; flagged in gaps file rather than silently corrected.

effective_anchorage_length_U_bars.description: Effective anchorage length (mm) measured from start of bend, for a U-bar (180-degree hook), by mandrel-size/bar-diameter ratio and bar size.

variables.mandrel_dia: bending mandrel diameter, expressed as a multiple of bar dia in the row index

minimum_overall_depth_U_bar_end_shapes.description: Minimum overall depth (dimension B) of U-bar end details, for two named end-shape styles ('Hook' and 'Trombone'), at fy=500 MPa.

hook_shape.geometry: 5-diameter lead-in (5d) into a bend of diameter B (the mandrel diameter)

trombone_shape.geometry: 5-diameter lead-in (5d), a 4-diameter offset (4d), into bend of diameter B (the mandrel diameter)

large_diameter_bends_minimum_mandrel_siz.description: Formula and derived lookup tables for the minimum bending mandrel diameter required for a bar under load at a bend, as a function of concrete strength class, spacing/cover parameter (ab), actual ultimate bar stress, and bar diameter.

formula.name: bm_min

variables.ab: half the pitch of bars, or nominal cover + b/2 (mm)
variables.fcd: design concrete strength = acc x fck / gamma_c (MPa)

formula.max_design_stress_note: Maximum design stress = characteristic yield stress / 1.15 = 435 MPa (for fyk=500)
formula.governing_note: Minimum mandrel size may instead be governed by the standard bend-radius rule: for bar size < 20mm, mandrel = 4b; for bar size >= 20mm, mandrel = 7b — whichever is larger governs.

precomputed_tables.status: NOT transcribed verbatim in this extraction
precomputed_tables.reason: Six large lookup tables are given in the source (one per concrete strength class: 20/25, 25/30, 28/35, 30/37, 32/40, 35/45 fck/fcu), each cross-tabulating ab (5 values: 25,50,75,100,150-and-over) x actual ultimate bar stress (8 rows: 100-450 MPa in 50 steps) x bar diameter (7 columns: 10,12,16,20,25,32,40mm) = up to 280 numeric cells per table, 1680+ cells total. Every cell is a direct numeric evaluation of the bm_min formula above (confirmed by spot-checking several cells against the formula). Since the formula, its variables, and the governing units are DIRECTLY STATED and complete, these tables are DERIVED/computable outputs and are represented in 10_generator.py as a callable function (`large_diameter_bend_mandrel()`) rather than reproduced as static data, to avoid an enormous low-value data dump. If a compiler needs the exact printed table values for validation/QA against the source (e.g. to catch OCR/print rounding), the raw table pages (183-188) should be re-OCR'd directly rather than relying on this extraction.

mandatory_shall: Neither A nor (free dim) shall be less than P (Table B.1) — applies to essentially every shape code.
No other shape code number, form of designation or abbreviation shall be used in scheduling (code 99 rule).
A dimensioned sketch shall be drawn over dimension columns A-E for shape 99; every dimension shall be specified; the tolerance-absorbing dimension shall be indicated in parentheses.
The length of straight between two bends shall be at least 4d.
recommendation_preferable: Note 1: near-90deg bends, it is preferable to specify shape code 99 with a fully dimensioned sketch.
practical_limits_may: Note 2: 5 bends or more may be impractical within permitted tolerances.
